name: מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק
summary: The king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who brought out bread and wine to Abram returning from the slaughter of the kings, blessed him, and received from him a tenth of all (Gen 14:18–20). Yahweh swears to David's lord, “you are a priest forever after the order of מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק” (Psa 110:4), and Hebrews applies the oath to Jesus, a high priest after his order and not after Aaron's, made so by the power of an indestructible life (Heb 5:6, 10; 7:11–17). The name is מֶלֶךְ “king” joined by ‑i to צֶדֶק “righteousness”, and scripture itself interprets it: “first, being interpreted, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace” (Heb 7:2).

evidence.note: “וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם brought out bread and wine, וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן.”
He blesses Abram by God Most High, and Abram gives him a tenth of everything.
“Yahweh has sworn and will not relent: You are a priest forever עַל דִּבְרָתִי מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק.”
“ἑρμηνευόμενος βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ὅ ἐστιν βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης”: the name read as king of righteousness.
Jesus entered as forerunner for us, “having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek”.
Another priest after Melchizedek's order, not Aaron's, shows the Levitical priesthood could not make perfect.

note: Formed from two roots, מלכ and צדק; filed under צדק (tsedeq) with the word צֶדֶק, since Hebrews interprets it as “king of righteousness” and the melek entry leaves personal names to names/. BDB's m.cd.aq is counted by spelling and so also takes צֶדֶק's own tokens (as a.be.ag does for Adoni-zedek); the name itself is Gen 14:18 and Psa 110:4, where the database writes it as two words מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק. The ‑i is read, as Hebrews reads it, as joining the two nouns, not as “my”.
